note: The originals (The Minimum Guarantees of Human Legal Subjecthood V3.0 / 100_POINT_EDITION, the MHEG theorem text, the fifteen principles of AI legal-logic governance) were not found. This catalogue is the one an earlier implementation of the user's (plato-audit-suite) carries; it has NOT been compared with the original and its names, definitions and independence are therefore PROVISIONAL. It is data: replacing it by the verified catalogue changes this file, not code.

guarantees.title: Subject Recognition and Score Non-Identity
guarantees.description: The person must not be treated as identical to a score, classification, prediction, or model output.

guarantees.title: Non-Reduction of Guarantees by Score
guarantees.description: A low score or adverse classification must not reduce access to notice, reasons, challenge, review, correction, suspension, remedy, or re-entry.

guarantees.title: AI Use and Decision Involvement Notice
guarantees.description: The person must be informed that AI was used, its purpose, its degree of influence, and the responsible institution.

guarantees.title: Current Score and Classification Access
guarantees.description: The person must be able to inspect their current score, classification, ranking, eligibility status, and risk status.

guarantees.title: Score History, Expiry, Purpose, and Sharing Access
guarantees.description: The person must be able to inspect score history, update reasons, validity period, purposes, recipients, and downstream uses.

guarantees.title: Legal Source and Institutional Basis Access
guarantees.description: The person must be able to identify the legislation, regulation, case law, contract, internal policy, guideline, or model policy used.

guarantees.title: Legal Concept Variable Transformation Access
guarantees.description: The person must be able to inspect how legal or institutional concepts were converted into variables, proxies, thresholds, weights, and computational rules.

guarantees.title: Separation of Facts, Inferences, Scores, and Normative Judgments
guarantees.description: The institution must clearly separate observed facts, inferred attributes, numerical scores, policy judgments, and legal conclusions.

guarantees.title: Individual Reasons and Inference Chain
guarantees.description: The person must receive individualised reasons and an intelligible account of the inferential chain leading to the decision.

guarantees.title: Correction of Data, Inferences, Scores, and Derived Records
guarantees.description: The person must be able to correct incorrect inputs, inferred attributes, scores, classifications, derived records, and propagated records.

guarantees.title: Contestation, Rebuttal, and Non-Discounting of Testimony
guarantees.description: The person must be able to contest the legal source, variable, proxy, inference, score, classification, and decision. Their testimony must not be automatically discounted because of a low score.

guarantees.title: Fair Burden of Proof and Independent Human Review
guarantees.description: The institution must not impose an excessive evidential burden on low-scoring subjects. Review must be performed by a human with authority to change or reverse the AI-mediated outcome.

guarantees.title: Suspension of Adverse Treatment and Score Use
guarantees.description: Where irreversible or serious harm may occur, the person must be able to request suspension of the decision, score use, or data sharing while review is pending.

guarantees.title: Reversible Treatment, Temporal Limitation, and Future Subjecthood
guarantees.description: Scores and classifications must have expiry, reassessment, correction, and deletion mechanisms. A present score must not permanently determine future legal or institutional status.

guarantees.title: Effective Re-entry, Support, Remedy, and Mutual Audit
guarantees.description: The person must have a realistic route back into the institution or opportunity, access to necessary procedural support, effective remedy for harm, and the ability to challenge the audit process itself.
